intro: When you work on contracts, your income can look uneven on paper, even when you're earning well. You're looking for a mortgage broker near you who understands day rates, contract gaps and how lenders assess contractor income. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK mortgage broker who can quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a contractor mortgage broker near me usually need
need_lead: You want someone local who can make sense of contractor income and present your situation to lenders in the right way.
needs: You're on a day rate and worried that a lender will average your income down or treat you as a higher risk than you are.
You've had gaps between contracts and want to know how those will be viewed before you apply.
You're newly self-employed through your own limited company and unsure which lenders will accept your trading history.
You want to buy a home or remortgage and need a broker who can explain how your contract rate translates into a borrowing figure.
You'd rather speak to someone face to face or by phone locally who deals with contractor cases regularly.
context_heading: Understanding how contractor income is assessed
context: Lenders don't all treat contractor income the same way. Some will annualise your day rate, others will look at your company accounts or tax returns, and some are more comfortable with contract gaps than others. A broker who works with contractors regularly will know which lenders take which approach and how to present your contracts and history clearly.

Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Any broker or adviser you use should be authorised, or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and you can check this on the FCA register. Brokers must also tell you whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you're a contractor and whether you work through a limited company, umbrella company or recruitment intermediary.
Give your current day rate and how long you've been contracting.
Explain any gaps between contracts and roughly how long they were.
Say whether you're looking to buy, remortgage or move home.
Include your approximate deposit or equity, if you have one in mind.
Mention your location so we can introduce you to a broker near you.

faqs.q: Can I get a mortgage if I've had gaps between contracts?
faqs.a: Yes, many contractors have gaps and still get mortgages. Lenders vary in how they view gaps, so a broker who knows contractor cases can point you to those more likely to accept your history.

faqs.q: Do I need to have been contracting for a certain length of time?
faqs.a: Some lenders want to see a trading history, while others may accept a current contract. A broker can tell you which lenders are more flexible for your situation.

faqs.q: How is my day rate used to work out what I can borrow?
faqs.a: Some lenders annualise your day rate, while others look at your company accounts or tax returns. Your broker will explain which approach each lender takes and how it affects your borrowing.

faqs.q: Is a contractor mortgage broker near me different from a high street broker?
faqs.a: A local broker who regularly deals with contractors will understand day rates, contract gaps and how to present your income. Being near you means you can meet in person if you prefer, but the advice should be the same wherever they are based.
